subject: MedIntel integration: model fit notes & guardrail plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@medintel.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@medintel.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery

Hi Samantha / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what I heard, and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs (from your team)
- Clinical triage summarization for inbound patient messages (short-form summaries, redaction of PHI fields)
- High safety/ refusal accuracy on medication advice and diagnosis (must refuse or escalate)
- Latency target for triage: edge cases OK up to 1.2s p99 for short messages, typical <800ms
- Throughput: ~250 reqs/min steady, spikes to 1.5k/min during certain hours

Immediate next steps I propose
1) We run a small model-fit eval (2–3 models) on a representative prompt set you provide — we can use our benchmark harness and return per-prompt safety/refusal signals.
2) Share a lightweight prompt and guardrail draft from our side for you to review (refusal templates, escalation triggers).
3) If model fit looks good, schedule an integration POC (Dedicated sandbox or Private) — timeline 3–4 weeks.

Deliverables from Redwood by next Wed (4/14):
- Benchmarked metrics (accuracy, refusal precision/recall on sensitive queries), latency/cost estimates
- A starter prompt set + suggested guardrail prompts (attached will be an initial set)
- Short action plan & integration checklist (attachment)

I attached a first pass of the benchmark outputs and the prompt set that our engineers used during the call. Please tell me if any of the sample prompts contain PHI — we'll redact on our side; we never store raw test data without explicit consent.

Proposed times for a short follow-up demo: Thu 4/15 10–11am PT or Mon 4/19 1–2pm PT — let me know what works.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0146

Attachments: medintel_benchmark_v2.csv (CSV, 78KB), medintel_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (JSONL, 12KB), integration_action_items.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@medintel.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@medintel.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the succinct recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
1) The 250 reqs/min is a conservative average — during peak hours we typically see 1.8k/min sustained for ~20 minutes. Hope that doesn't change your recommendations drastically.
2) For safety, our bar is that the model must refuse when confidence in a medical recommendation is low and surface a "clinician escalation" path. We can share 120 labeled prompts (non-PHI) by Monday.
3) Latency is important but we'd prefer prioritized safety over shaving 100–200ms.

Can you confirm which model variants you'll run in the fit eval and whether you anticipate the need for quantized variants for Dedicated vs Private? Also pls confirm that Redwood can support KM/zero-logging for the POC (we'll need an NDA & SOC2 evidence).

Samantha
Samantha Li, Head of Product
MedIntel Health
samantha.li@medintel.com | (617) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@medintel.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@medintel.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery

Thanks Samantha — great context. Short answers up front: we can handle 1.8k/min spikes with a Dedicated pool sized as discussed; quantized variants are available for dedicated/private to reduce cost and maintain acceptable latency; we support a zero-logging POC and can share SOC2 docs (link below).

Models we'll run in the initial fit eval (suggested):
- redwood-open-7B-v2-finetune (float16) — good balance of safety and latency
- redwood-13B-std (int8 quantized) — higher coverage on complex prompts, slightly higher latency
- redwood-safety-lite-3B (fast refuser baseline) — purpose-built to maximize refusal precision on disallowed medical advice

What we'll deliver in the fit eval:
- Per-prompt pass/fail on refusal behavior (precision, recall, and examples of false positives/negatives)
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) measured on your sample prompt set (we'll run at your expected RPS)
- Cost estimate per 1M tokens and estimated unit cost per request for both Dedicated and Private deployment options
- Regression checklist: we will run pre/post quantization checks, and flag any >5% drop in refusal recall or >3% increase in unsafe outputs

Safety/guardrails (initial suggestions):
- Refusal templates: "I can't provide medical advice. Please consult a licensed clinician. If this is urgent, call [local emergency number]."
- Escalation triggers: presence of medication names + action verb (e.g. "start", "stop", "increase dose"), mention of self-harm, or requests to interpret test results in a way that results in a medical action.
- Prompt-level classifier: first-stage lightweight classifier to tag potentially disallowed prompts; second-stage model for generation with hard refusal boundary.

Benchmarks / links (examples)
- MedIntel benchmark CSV (sanitized): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/medintel/benchmarks/medintel_benchmark_v2.csv
- Prompt library & starter guardrails: https://docs.redwood.com/shared/medintel/prompt-library
- SOC2 evidence (read-only link): https://security.redwood.com/soc2/report-2026

Attachment note: medintel_prompt_set_v1.jsonl is a sanitized sample we used during the call. Please confirm you want us to run on the 120 labeled prompts you mentioned — we'll queue that as "MedIntel-fit-202704" in our harness.

Proposed schedule
- Thu 4/15: short walk-through of the starter benchmarks (30m)
- Mon 4/19–Fri 4/23: run full fit eval on your labeled prompts; deliver results by Mon 4/26

I'll schedule the 4/15 slot — sending an invite.

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: medintel_benchmark_v2.csv, medintel_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, integration_action_items.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MedIntel fit eval — need safety review + guardrail prompts

Marissa / Evelyn — forwarding the thread with materials from MedIntel. They're ready to hand us a 120-prompt labeled set next week; they require very high refusal precision on medication/diagnosis prompts and a clear clinician-escalation UX.

Ask for you both:
- Marissa: can you review the attached prompt set and the redwood-safety-lite-3B baseline? Please call out any immediate holes in the refusal templates and whether the escalation triggers above are sufficient.
- Evelyn: can you run the quick evaluation checklist (refusal precision target >= 92%, false refusal rate <= 6%) against the sample and propose 3 guardrail prompt rewrites that increase safety without greatly hurting recall?

Notes / concerns to consider: 
- Quantization risk: if we move redwood-13B to int8 for Dedicated, we need to validate refusal behavior doesn't degrade beyond our regression threshold (>5% drop). Please prioritize any tests that exercise medication dose-change requests and ambiguous test-result interpretation.
- UX: recommend the second-stage classifier wedge to reduce false rejections of benign administrative questions (e.g., appointment times).

I've attached the sanitized prompt set and our benchmark CSV. Forwarding full thread below for context. If you prefer, we can triage in a 30-minute huddle this afternoon.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround on this (target EOD Thu 4/15).

Best,
Ben
